# Mídas walks into a finance, wealth & commerce firm

The finance, wealth & commerce world does not cite Mídas in its documentation. It does not need to — it performs the archetype daily, unbilled.

## Before the Office, the Story

**Silenos Returned.** Silenos, the drunken companion of Dionysos, strayed and was brought to Mídas — in some tellings caught in the king's own rose gardens.  Mídas entertained him ten days and returned him to the god, who offered any gift in thanks.  The king, thinking of his treasury, wished that everything he touched might become gold.

**All He Touches Turns to Gold.** The gift revealed itself at table: the bread stiffened in his hands, the wine ran molten and would not wet his lips.  Hungry and thirsty in a house of gold, Mídas begged release.  Dionysos sent him to wash in the spring of the Pactolus at Sardis; the power passed from his body into the river, whose sands bore gold ever after.

- **Temple:** Mídas

- **Sectors touched:** Commerce & Governance · Home & Lifestyle · Energy & Natural World · Culture & Entertainment

## The Reveal, Seat by Seat

### Finance, Wealth & Commerce

*Wealth personified — the name every gold fund wishes it owned.* Nobody in that trade worships at this temple. They just keep its hours.

### Gems, Jewelry & Luxury Materials

*The golden touch itself; the precious metal made myth.* Nobody in that trade worships at this temple. They just keep its hours.

### Agriculture, Food & Harvest

Now read the why-line with the office in mind: *Herodotus records the sixty-petaled roses of Phrygia — a horticultural legend (8.138).* The people doing this work did not borrow the archetype. They re-derived it — the way Mídas was always going to be re-derived wherever king of phrygia, the golden touch matters.

### Startups & Venture Creation

*The touch that turns all to gold — value creation, with its caution built in.* Nobody in that trade worships at this temple. They just keep its hours.

### Wine, Brewing & Hospitality

*He hosted Silenos with wine and was granted the wish — hospitality that returned a thousandfold.* Nobody in that trade worships at this temple. They just keep its hours.

## Not the First Rebrand

Mídas absorbed no foreign gods; instead, the myth absorbed the man.  Greek storytellers took a historical Phrygian dynasty and hung upon it their two great parables of appetite and judgment. The office is only the latest translation.
